question: What latitude/longitude should represent each pooled region (NE, SE, Alley, Offshore) for mapping?
context: Samples are pooled across stations into 4 regions defined by the CalCOFI grid (Hayward & Venrick 1998), so there is no per-station position. Need a representative centroid (or grid-cell set) per region to place observations on the datacheck/schema maps. Superseded in part: the six off-grid stations are no longer an obstacle (calcofi4db 3.16.0 cc_station_regions() + cc_calcofi_to_lonlat()), so the remaining ask is whether the membership is still current. Dropped from blocker to high on 2026-08-14 for that reason.
proposed_answer: RESOLVED in the repo, pending only your confirmation of the station lists. definitions.xlsx sheet `Regions` defines each region as an explicit list of CalCOFI stations (Hayward & Venrick 1998), so we no longer invent a position - we derive the geometry from that membership. Two things changed since this was filed. (1) All 34 declared stations now place. The six we reported as missing - 83.41, 83.51, 90.37, 77.51, 80.51, 90.53 - are intermediate inshore stations with no cell in the regularized grid, but they are perfectly good CalCOFI coordinates: `+proj=calcofi` is a projection, not a lookup, so it resolves them exactly. Three of the six are NE`s, which was the case we were most worried about. Extending the grid reference is therefore NOT needed. (2) Each region is now a POLYGON, not a centroid. A convex hull over the member stations turned out wrong in three ways - SE`s four stations are collinear on line 93.3 so its hull is a 73 km2 sliver, NE and Alley overlap by 19.8 km2, and the hulls leave 44,616 km2 of the pooled domain (a third of it) in no region at all. So each station instead claims the water nearest to it and the cells are dissolved by region: the four regions tile their domain exactly, no overlap and no gaps, each one connected. Areas: Alley 44,843 km2, Offshore 59,452, NE 21,263, SE 9,836. The outer boundary is the convex hull of the stations themselves - we do not pad it outward, because the pooling says nothing about water beyond the outermost station occupied. `phyto_sample` keeps a single point, now a representative point guaranteed to fall INSIDE its own region rather than a centroid (these regions are concave - Alley wraps around NE - so a centroid can land in the neighbour). What we still need from you: the sheet predates the later cruises, so please confirm the four station lists describe the pooling for the whole 1996-2022 series, or tell us where membership changed.

question: Some observations in this dataset resolve no CalCOFI grid cell. Are these positions genuinely off-grid (transit, historical stations outside the modern pattern), a coarser spatial notion with no point position, or a coordinate error?
context: 159,804 of    159,804 obs rows (100.00%) resolve no CalCOFI grid cell;      0 of those carry no latitude/longitude at all. These are now RELEASED rather than dropped. Are they off-grid positions (transit, historical stations), a coarser spatial notion (region-pooled), or a coordinate error?
proposed_answer: Until v2026.08.10 these rows were DROPPED from `obs` entirely by a `WHERE grid_key IS NOT NULL` filter, while their sampling events stayed in `sample` — so the dataset silently lost them. They are now released with a NULL grid_key. We are not proposing to re-exclude them; we need to know which of the three cases applies so the metadata can say so. A coordinate error is the one that matters most: the sign-flipped Longitude_W on five CalCOFI cruises was invisible precisely because being off-grid removed the rows without a trace.
answer: Answered by the dataset's own design, not by the provider: calcofi_phytoplankton is REGION-POOLED (EDI knb-lter-cce.254.4). A sample is a pooled region, not a station occupation, so there is no point position to resolve and grid_key is NULL for all 159,804 rows by construction. This is the 'coarser spatial notion' case, and it is the precedent for releasing ungridded observations rather than an exception to it: this dataset has emitted them since it landed. No action.
